answer_to_question: Yes to all three questions, each re-derived by running the real gate against mutated coverage.py rather than accepting the packet's evidence. Baseline first: ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --tests binjava.CoverageGateTest reports tests=14 failures=0 errors=0. Then four mutations, each applied to scripts/coverage.py, run with --rerun-tasks, and reverted (final sha256 of scripts/coverage.py equals the pre-mutation backup, 5e8e0106..., so the staged bytes are untouched). (1) TR3 CLOSED: c.get('BRANCH', (0, 0)) -> (91, 100) is killed by aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage at CoverageGateTest.java:208, the new contains("branch 100.0%") assertion -- the gate prints 'branch  91.0%' and still exits 0, so exit status alone would have survived exactly as the prior round said. (2) TR5 CLOSED, and the rationale that replaced the false one is TRUE: restoring 'and not p.startswith(\'buildSrc/\')' in the module comprehension is killed by buildSrcIsMeasuredLikeAnyOtherModule at :236. The deletion is also justified against this tree, verified independently of the test: buildSrc/src/main contains only kotlin, buildSrc/build/classes/java contains only 'test', and glob('buildSrc/build/classes/java/main/**/*.class') returns [] -- so has_classes is False and the loop already skipped buildSrc. The filter was dead, and the prior javadoc's 'fails EVERY commit' claim was false as the prior round said. (3) The NEW test's own rationale holds and it is not redundant with the existing exclusion test: moving 'measured += 1' back above 'if m in skips' is killed ONLY by anExcludedModuleIsNotCountedAsMeetingTheFloors at :258, with the exact false sentence the javadoc names -- 'WARN format line 10.0% branch 10.0% EXCLUDED: ...' followed by 'ok 1 module(s) meet 95% line / 90% branch', exit 0. The pre-existing honoursAnExclusionListedInTheBaseline survives that mutation untouched because it asserts only startsWith("0"), so the bug was real and was invisible to the suite before this round. 'if skipped:' -> 'if False:' is killed by the same test at :264 (contains 'every module with classes is excluded'), so the third-fact distinction is separately pinned, not carried by one assertion. One extra probe of my own, to check the second new assertion at :210 is not inert: inserting 'if BRANCH not in c: continue' before line_cov is killed at :208 rather than :210, so :210 is partially redundant against that mutation -- but deleting 'measured += 1' outright is caught by :210 (and by passesAboveTheFloors' doesNotContain("NOT-MEASURED")), so it is not dead weight. No assertion in the delta was loosened: every change adds a constraint (:208, :210, :256-265) or inverts one to match a behaviour whose old form rested on dead code, and coverage.py's only test-visible change is the deletion the reviewer asked for. TR4 and TR6 not re-reported as findings per the round's scope -- but see TR7, which is about the mechanism of that deferral rather than about either finding.

findings.summary: The deferral of TR4 and TR6 is recorded as backlog IDs M0.42 and M0.43, and neither ID exists. `git grep 'M0\.4[23]'` over the whole tracked tree returns nothing, and the highest ID in the staged backlog is M0.41. The three OTHER deferrals made by this same commit (M0.39, M0.40, M0.41) each got a real backlog row in the staged diff; these two got a commit-message reference only. So the two findings the round agreed to carry forward are recorded nowhere in the tree.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a surviving mutation -- this is a traceability defect, and it is the exact one review.sh:105-108 already names in its own source ('a finding vanished into a gitignored directory'). Concretely: the commit lands; .harness/review/ is gitignored and local to this machine; check-cross-refs.sh, the gate that would catch a dangling M<n> citation, is M0.20 and does not exist; check-commit-msg.sh validates only the SUBJECT against the backlog, so a body citing M0.42 is unchecked. The next session greps for M0.42, finds nothing, and both findings are gone -- TR4 (`p.count('/') == 1` is constrained by no fixture, because every module() call creates a direct child of the fixture root, so deleting the clause leaves all 14 green) and TR6 (all 14 red records are NoSuchFileException at CoverageGateTest.java:33, i.e. 'the gate is absent', which a body of assertThat(gate(repo)).isNotNull() would produce identically). Deferring both is right on the merits and I am not contesting it; what does not hold is a commit message asserting they were recorded when the referenced rows were never written, which is non-negotiable 4 in miniature. Fix is two backlog rows in the style of the M0.39-M0.41 ones already in this diff, or renumbering the citation to whatever IDs those rows get. Rated minor because it costs nothing in test strength: all 14 tests pass, all four claimed mutations are separated by the tests that claim them, and the M0.13 acceptance criterion -- the gate exists and refuses correctly -- has a failing-without-the-change test for every refusal path (below either floor independently, exactly at the floor, classes with no report, unreadable report, counterless report, unregenerated report, regeneration failure, all-excluded tree).
